subject: history_social
passage: Dholavira, a Harappan city built more than 4,000 years ago on an island in the salt flats of the Rann of Kutch in present-day Gujarat, India, received little rain, and the two streams that flowed past it ran for only part of the year. To get through the long dry months, the city's residents cut a series of large reservoirs into the bedrock and built dams and channels on the streams to steer the seasonal runoff into ______. Archaeologists regard this system as one of the most sophisticated examples of water management in the ancient world.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The runoff was steered into the things built to hold water: "a series of large reservoirs." That antecedent is plural ("reservoirs"), so the pronoun must be the plural object pronoun "them." Don't be pulled toward a singular noun closer to the blank, such as "bedrock" or "runoff"; runoff can't be steered into bedrock or into itself.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Itself" is a singular reflexive pronoun; the sentence would say the runoff was steered into the runoff, and it doesn't match the plural "reservoirs."
explanation.B: Incorrect. "It" is singular, but the water was steered into the plural "reservoirs."
explanation.C: Correct. The plural pronoun "them" refers back to the plural antecedent "reservoirs."
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Its" is a possessive form, which must be followed by a noun ("its banks"); it can't stand alone as the object of "into."
